rationale: Evidence: 0 of 180 development trials finished across iterations 0 to 3. Every run ended off track at progress 0.04 to 0.15, with max_error at the 0.06 m off-track limit. Iteration 0 (kp 3.0, kd 0.5, ki 0.05, base 1.6, 12 mm sensors at y=0.04, span +/-0.04) scored best at 53.0. The s-bend progress stuck at 0.1475 across iterations 0, 1 and 2 despite changes to kp, kd, base_speed, sensor size, sensor span and track width. That points to a failure that none of those levers touched, so I am not chasing it with more of the same. Iteration 3 cut kp to 2.5 and moved sensors back to y=0.03, and it fell to 35.5 (s-bend progress 0.043). So lower kp and sensors set further back both hurt. Iteration 2 (kp 4.5, kd 1.0) also did worse than iteration 0, so higher gain alone is not the fix. Changes from iteration 0, kept small so the next race attributes any gain: (1) kp 3.0 to 3.5, a modest step up, since kp below 3 has clearly hurt and kp 4.5 with 0.016 sensors was not better. (2) kd 0.5 to 0.8 for more damping of the stronger correction. (3) ki 0.05 to 0.0, removing integral action, since it has not helped and can wind up on bends. (4) base_speed 1.6 to 1.5, a small cut for more correction time at bends, which costs little progress. Geometry is kept identical to iteration 0 so the controller effect is isolated. Expected result: progress somewhat above 0.15 on the s-bend and oval with max_error nearer 0.05 m; a score near or modestly above 53. Completion remains unlikely, since 1.5 m/s average is needed for the 3 s limit.
